item.description:
The iPad as a lighting wing, and touch screens

  • iPad lighting wing: turn on the phone remote (Setup → MIDI, OSC, Timecode & Phone Remote), open the /wing address it shows on the iPad and enter the PIN. Groups, palettes, keys and encoders by touch; everything happens on the Mac at once.
  • Touch mode for touch monitors (Lighting → Tools → Touch Screen): finger-sized keys, tiles and knobs, and ADD / REMOVE keys in place of ⇧ and ⌘.
  • Programming screen: smaller palette tiles, a roomier keypad, the selection tools above the groups, the encoders as devices along the bottom with a Programmer device (Fan, record mask, time, Blind).

A new lighting programming screen, and editing on the waveform

  • Lighting, Program view: MagicQ's layout with grandMA3's look. Groups, colour, position, beam and FX palettes; MagicQ's keys on the right; the selection tools (Odd, Even, 1 in 3, Invert, Reverse, Rem Dim…) above the groups.
  • Encoders along the bottom, as devices (Intensity, Position, Colour, Beam) with a Programmer device for Fan, record mask, time and Blind.
  • Same keys everywhere: click uses a group or palette, ⇧ adds, ⌘ takes away, ⌥ stores. A line at the bottom says what anything under the mouse does.
  • Move in Black has a time per cue and finishes before the lights come on.
  • Sound: edit right on the waveform under a cue (no Edit mode): drag across to select, then Cut & Join, Silence or Gain; drag the white line to change the level. The waveform keeps its size.
  • Level line tools after Ableton: drag a segment, stretch and tilt handles, shapes, Simplify, Z/X zoom, R reverse, ⌘E split.

Sound editing, effects and the level line

  • Level line: in Trim & Loop, click Edit, drag across a stretch, then drag the line up or down.
  • Quick edits: select a stretch and right-click for Delete, Silence, Gain, Fades, Reverse, Copy/Paste, Split, Render to a New File.
  • Effects tab: EQ, filter, reverb, delay, compressor, limiter, pitch, distortion and Audio Unit plug-ins, with presets and Freeze.
  • Lighting: the Program view has a pan/tilt pad and an on-screen keypad; the visualiser has its own window.
